content: Both linezolid and serotonergic drugs increase serotonin levels. If linezolid must be administered, discontinue serotonergic drugs immediately and monitor for central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Serotonergic therapy can be resumed 24 hours after the last dose of linezolid or after two weeks of monitoring, whichever occurs first. Linezolid may increase serotonin levels due to its monoamine oxidase A (MAO-A) inhibition. This interaction can lead to serotonin syndrome, characterized by mental status changes, autonomic instability, and neuromuscular hyperactivity. Avoid co-administration of linezolid with serotonergic drugs or use alternative therapies. Linezolid can increase the toxicity of certain drugs, such as opioids (e.g., morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl) and other serotonergic agents, through unknown mechanisms or pharmacodynamic synergism. This may result in severe adverse effects, including hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Separate administration of these drugs by at least 14 days if possible. Linezolid interacts with various medications by altering their metabolism or pharmacodynamics. For example, it can decrease the efficacy of oral contraceptives and live bacterial vaccines by altering intestinal flora. It can also increase the effects of beta-agonists (e.g., salmeterol, terbutaline) and anesthetics (e.g., etomidate), potentially leading to acute hypertensive episodes or enhanced sedation. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these agents. Linezolid may enhance dopamine blockade when combined with antipsychotics (e.g., clozapine, aripiprazole), increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Symptoms include hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, and autonomic dysfunction. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity or neuroleptic malignant syndrome during co-administration. In cases where linezolid is co-administered with drugs that lower the seizure threshold (e.g., amifampridine), the risk of seizures may increase. Similarly, co-administration with myelosuppressive agents (e.g., ropeginterferon alfa-2b) may lead to additive myelosuppression. Monitor patients closely for these risks. Linezolid is contraindicated with certain drugs, such as triptans (e.g., sumatriptan, rizatriptan, zolmitriptan), due to the risk of serotonin syndrome and decreased metabolism of these agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. In summary, linezolid has significant interactions with serotonergic drugs, opioids, antipsychotics, and other agents, necessitating careful monitoring or avoidance of co-administration. Always assess the risk of serotonin syndrome, CNS toxicity, and other adverse effects when prescribing linezolid in combination with other medications.
